sentence: This project studies how crossovers between maternal and paternal chromosomes are established in mammalian meiosis and what regulates their spread across the genome.
This project builds atlases that show how the dorsal aspect of human visual cortex develops in childhood, both in function and in structure.
This project uses models of uterine cancer to study how changing risk factors affect incidence and mortality, and how screening and treatment strategies work.
This project studies how education quantity and quality affect cognition and the risk of dementia, and what role genetics plays in that link.
This project builds a way to tell cancer from other lesions of the mouth using a brush sample, without surgery.
This project studies how a long non-coding RNA found only in females makes T cells cause disease in a mouse model of Crohn's Disease.
This project studies what a signaling protein does in fat, liver and muscle by turning it on in each tissue and tracking its genes.
This project runs a shared facility that offers flow cytometry services such as cell sorting and image analysis to cancer researchers.
This project studies how neural circuits in the medial entorhinal cortex, a brain region tied to navigation and memory, work in a healthy brain.
This project builds 3D structural models of enzymes that cause mutations in cancer and uses them to work toward inhibiting those mutations.
This project uses machine learning and other computer models to study how features of host and pathogen together shape disease outcomes.
This project studies how people who use drugs experience xylazine and builds a computer program that finds emergency department patients exposed to it.
This project tests ways to add cervical cancer screening and treatment to HIV care for women living with HIV, using a randomized trial.
This project tries to find out what role bacteria play in the growth of calcium-based kidney stones.
This project provides microscopes and expert help so researchers can study the anatomy and cell biology of fixed and live tissues.
This project uses AI models to predict how phages interact with bacteria, to help design tests of phage therapy against Klebsiella pneumoniae.
This project uses cues from fetal liver hematopoietic stem cells to build culture systems outside the body that help these cells engraft better.
This project uses engineered models of tumor invasion to find drugs and to test whether blocking genes involved in breast cancer spread can suppress invasion.
This project uses engineered islet cells, blood vessels and immune cells from patients to study how type 1 diabetes starts and progresses in humanized mice.
This project builds low-touch interventions to improve outcomes for telemedicine users of HIV preexposure prophylaxis and tests them in randomized, controlled trials.
